result.title: Do the Details Help the Whole? One-Way Transfer from Person Actions to Group Intent in VLMs on JRDB-Social
result.summary: Social scene datasets label people at two levels: what each person is doing and what the group is there for. Training on both levels at once is often assumed to help each of them. We test this assumption for vision-language models (VLMs) on JRDB-Social, treating person actions as the details and group intent as the whole. We fine-tune Qwen3.5 4B under eight training arms with three seeds, repeat the core arms on Qwen3.5 9B and Qwen3-VL 4B, and judge every arm with a verdict rule fixed before testing. Writing each member's actions before the intent raises intent macro-F1 from 30.1 to 31.0, and writing the intent first reaches 31.2, while action F1 stays within 0.2 points of an action-only model. Under the selected recipe, no arm trained with intent improves actions. The gain requires correct, image-grounded actions: empty action lists or actions borrowed from another group with the same intent lower intent F1. Forced-prefix tests, occlusion, member masking, linear probes and component grafting show that the intent follows the written actions, relies more on people and partly resides in the vision tower. Supplying actions as input instead of as targets hurts both levels.

AI.brief_summary: 在 JRDB-Social 上对 Qwen3.5 4B/9B 与 Qwen3-VL 4B 做八组训练臂、多种子微调，检验「先写出个体动作再预测群体意图」这类细节到整体的单向迁移是否成立，并用强制前缀、遮挡、成员掩码、线性探针与组件移植做因果核查。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及视觉细节是否被真正使用、中间步骤对最终答案的因果贡献与视觉塔依赖，与 LVR 的信息保留和贡献分配问题相关；不过其中间状态以显式文本动作呈现，可作为 latent 内容使用与否的对照设计参考，但不能直接外推到 latent 推理。
